The description states: “The reactor (working volume, 38 L; Fig. 1 ) had 1.6 m working height and 0.15 m internal diameter. The inside temperature was kept constant to the mesophilic condition (35 ± 1 °C), using water jacket. Nitrogen was purged for 5 min to guarantee the anaerobic environment (dissolved oxygen concentration at ∼0.1 mg/L). The reactor was seeded with sludge (10 L) collected from a local wastewater treatment plant between filter pressing and dewatering processes, followed by the continuous feeding of synthetic wastewater (with COD, 500 mg/L; TN, 40 mg/L; and TP, 10 mg/L), similar to the local domestic wastewater, at the hydraulic retention time (HRT) of 10 days and 35 °C to start up the reactor for the sludge maturation/granulation.” The text does not explicitly state that the reactor was designed or operated *specifically* to utilize biogas bubbles for self-flotation or solid-liquid separation. It simply describes the reactor as a UASB reactor, which inherently involves sludge blanket formation and the presence of bubbles. The description focuses on the operational parameters and the function of the sludge blanket, not a deliberate design for self-flotation.
